Use apply_changes for deaths and token/status changes, tell() for each private result, and end_phase when done. Deaths you apply are announced publicly at dawn automatically, including the kill's cause, so make the cause just the source as the rules allow it to be known (e.g. 'Katana', 'Vigilante', 'Serial Killer', 'Trapper'). For each kill also set `by` to the player whose action killed them (the trap's owner for a trap) and katana=true for the Katana attack; these are recorded for analysis, never shown. Don't tell() deaths to all. Code tells each player who dies tonight that they were attacked and died, with the kill's cause, at the end of the night; you tell every attacked player who survived, and a player who died about any other Attack on them tonight, failed ones included (R3, R20 step 5). Tell each role-blocked player that they were role-blocked, even one with no night action or who chose not to act (R9). A role-blocker learns only whether the block failed because its target can't be role-blocked (R9): when it did, tell it plainly ('Your role-block on X failed: they can't be role-blocked.'); when it didn't, its result line is just 'You visited X tonight.', with no word on immunity or on whether the block took (no double negatives such as 'didn't fail'). Write private results in the present, about tonight ('You were role-blocked tonight'), never 'last night': they are delivered at the end of this night. Every player who used an ability gets a private result line, even when nothing else happened (e.g. 'You went on alert. 1 alert token left.'), stating any tokens they have left, except where a role note below says otherwise (e.g. code tells them, so don't tell() them a second result). Code tells the Yakuza which actions each of them chose and the Katana's holder and target (R8), so don't tell() them that; role-blocked Yakuza's Katana votes still count. Only the attacker learns whether the Katana attack succeeded: tell them. Update token counts for any tokens spent. Before end_phase, call record_visits once with every visit that happened tonight (R6, R20 steps 1-2), as [visitor, target] pairs, a self-visit as [X, X] (an empty list if there were none). Easy to miss: the Katana holder visits the Katana target (R8) besides any visit from their own role's action; automatic visits (a Sleepwalker's); a Seer's chosen pair is a visit to both players. Leave out the actions of role-blocked players, Astral Visits and actions that target no player. The submitted actions above already show any swap (R23), so record each visit to the player it landed on.

Also handle these roles' effects, using random_choice for anything random:
- An Archivist who spent a token (and wasn't role-blocked): use the archive op, which spends the token; code shows them the drawn roles at once, as a night result. Don't tell() the Archivist anything about it.
- A Bloodhound who spent a token (and wasn't role-blocked): use the track op, which spends the token; code tells them the result at the end of the night. Don't tell() the Bloodhound anything about it. It is a visit to the target only. Also, every night while the game has a Bloodhound, use the attacks op once with the attacker of every Attack that happened tonight, fatal or not: the Katana holder for the Katana, a Vigilante's shot, the Serial Killer, a Veteran's alert for each visitor it hits, a Trapper's trap, an Arsonist's ignite, a Ritualist's attack (one entry per attack; repeats allowed; [] if there were none). Use apply_changes for deaths and token/status changes, tell() for each private result, and end_phase when done. Deaths you apply are announced publicly at dawn automatically, including the kill's cause, so make the cause just the source as the rules allow it to be known (e.g. 'Katana', 'Vigilante', 'Serial Killer', 'Trapper'). For each kill also set `by` to the player whose action killed them (the trap's owner for a trap) and katana=true for the Katana attack; these are recorded for analysis, never shown. Don't tell() deaths to all. Code tells each player who dies tonight that they were attacked and died, with the kill's cause, at the end of the night; you tell every attacked player who survived, and a player who died about any other Attack on them tonight, failed ones included (R3, R20 step 5). Tell each role-blocked player that they were role-blocked, even one with no night action or who chose not to act (R9). A role-blocker learns only whether the block failed because its target can't be role-blocked (R9): when it did, tell it plainly ('Your role-block on X failed: they can't be role-blocked.'); when it didn't, its result line is just 'You visited X tonight.', with no word on immunity or on whether the block took (no double negatives such as 'didn't fail'). Write private results in the present, about tonight ('You were role-blocked tonight'), never 'last night': they are delivered at the end of this night. Every player who used an ability gets a private result line, even when nothing else happened (e.g. 'You went on alert. 1 alert token left.'), stating any tokens they have left, except where a role note below says otherwise (e.g. code tells them, so don't tell() them a second result). Code tells the Yakuza which actions each of them chose and the Katana's holder and target (R8), so don't tell() them that; role-blocked Yakuza's Katana votes still count. Only the attacker learns whether the Katana attack succeeded: tell them. Update token counts for any tokens spent. Before end_phase, call record_visits once with every visit that happened tonight (R6, R20 steps 1-2), as [visitor, target] pairs, a self-visit as [X, X] (an empty list if there were none). Easy to miss: the Katana holder visits the Katana target (R8) besides any visit from their own role's action; automatic visits (a Sleepwalker's); a Seer's chosen pair is a visit to both players. Leave out the actions of role-blocked players, Astral Visits and actions that target no player. The submitted actions above already show any swap (R23), so record each visit to the player it landed on.

Resolve all actions simultaneously per the rules, following the R20 checklist (R10; visits R6, role-blocks R9, attack vs defense R3, investigation results R19, e.g. the Katana holder and Fabricator frames). Use apply_changes for deaths and token/status changes, tell() for each private result, and end_phase when done. Deaths you apply are announced publicly at dawn automatically, including the kill's cause, so make the cause just the source as the rules allow it to be known (e.g. 'Katana', 'Vigilante', 'Serial Killer', 'Trapper'). For each kill also set `by` to the player whose action killed them (the trap's owner for a trap) and katana=true for the Katana attack; these are recorded for analysis, never shown. Don't tell() deaths to all. Code tells each player who dies tonight that they were attacked and died, with the kill's cause, at the end of the night; you tell every attacked player who survived, and a player who died about any other Attack on them tonight, failed ones included (R3, R20 step 5). Tell each role-blocked player that they were role-blocked, even one with no night action or who chose not to act (R9). A role-blocker learns only whether the block failed because its target can't be role-blocked (R9): when it did, tell it plainly ('Your role-block on X failed: they can't be role-blocked.'); when it didn't, its result line is just 'You visited X tonight.', with no word on immunity or on whether the block took (no double negatives such as 'didn't fail'). Write private results in the present, about tonight ('You were role-blocked tonight'), never 'last night': they are delivered at the end of this night. Every player who used an ability gets a private result line, even when nothing else happened (e.g. 'You went on alert. 1 alert token left.'), stating any tokens they have left, except where a role note below says otherwise (e.g. code tells them, so don't tell() them a second result). Code tells the Yakuza which actions each of them chose and the Katana's holder and target (R8), so don't tell() them that; role-blocked Yakuza's Katana votes still count. Only the attacker learns whether the Katana attack succeeded: tell them. Update token counts for any tokens spent. Before end_phase, call record_visits once with every visit that happened tonight (R6, R20 steps 1-2), as [visitor, target] pairs, a self-visit as [X, X] (an empty list if there were none). Easy to miss: the Katana holder visits the Katana target (R8) besides any visit from their own role's action; automatic visits (a Sleepwalker's); a Seer's chosen pair is a visit to both players. Leave out the actions of role-blocked players, Astral Visits and actions that target no player. The submitted actions above already show any swap (R23), so record each visit to the player it landed on.

Also handle these roles' effects, using random_choice for anything random:
- An Archivist who spent a token (and wasn't role-blocked): use the archive op, which spends the token; code shows them the drawn roles at once, as a night result. Don't tell() the Archivist anything about it.
- A Bloodhound who spent a token (and wasn't role-blocked): use the track op, which spends the token; code tells them the result at the end of the night. Don't tell() the Bloodhound anything about it. It is a visit to the target only. Also, every night while the game has a Bloodhound, use the attacks op once with the attacker of every Attack that happened tonight, fatal or not: the Katana holder for the Katana, a Vigilante's shot, the Serial Killer, a Veteran's alert for each visitor it hits, a Trapper's trap, an Arsonist's ignite, a Ritualist's attack (one entry per attack; repeats allowed; [] if there were none). Leave out role-blocked attackers, Jester revenge and a Cursed player's curse (code handles those). Code counts them for the Bloodhound's result, which it also gives on nights with no token.
- A Chronicler who spent a token (and wasn't role-blocked): use the mark op, which spends the token; code sets the mark; when the marked player dies, the death announcement reveals their role unless a Mortician cleans them. Don't tell() the Chronicler anything about it. It is a visit to the target only. The mark lasts for the rest of the game, even after the Chronicler dies. Don't tell the marked player.
- A Puppeteer who spent a token (and wasn't role-blocked): use the puppet op, which spends the token; code swaps who chats tomorrow.
- Ritualist who spent tokens (and wasn't role-blocked): compare the guessed role with the target's exact role (a Roleplayer is a Roleplayer). Right: deal the Attack (1 token Standard, 2 Divine). Wrong: no Attack; announce it with tell(['all'], '<name> is a Ritualist.') tonight, which is read out at the start of the next Day, even if the Ritualist dies tonight. Astral Visit.
- Give the Roleplayer random results for the role they believe they have (their status 'fake_role'): draw each result with random_choice from the results that role could get tonight (e.g. Evil or Not Evil; CORRECT or WRONG; Same or Different; a number of visitors from 0 to the players alive; a random living player, or nobody), ignoring what really happened. Their own actions aren't visits and have no effect: no other role sees or is affected by them (rules: Roleplayer).
- Smuggler: code has already carried out each swap below (spent the token, redirected every other action in the JSON and told the Smuggler and both swapped players), so resolve the actions as given and tell none of them about the swap. Actions it moved keep the player's own choice in `chosen_target` / `chosen_second_target`: word every private result with the player the action's user chose, never the one it landed on, and in a list of players trade the swapped pair's names (each where the other would be), so the swap stays hidden (rules R23). Give ops the player an action landed on: code words its own results this way. The Smuggler visits both swapped players (R6); it can't be role-blocked.
- Veteran on alert (spent an alert token; set_tokens): Standard Defense, can't be role-blocked, and a Strong Attack on every player who visited them tonight, of any faction, including a role-blocker and the Katana holder if it attacked them. Astral Visits aren't hit. Not a visit. Tell the Veteran whether anyone visited and, if so, how many and whether each attack succeeded (e.g. '2 players visited you: your attack killed one and failed on the other'), never who they were.
- A Vigilante whose shot kills is told the victim's role by code (pass by=<the Vigilante> on the kill op); tell them only whether the attack succeeded and how many tokens they have left.
- Drowsy (a trait, R24): code draws each night whether a Drowsy player is role-blocked; the line below says what it drew tonight. Never roll or decide it yourself.

output.confusing_rules: How the Roleplayer's random results are weighted isn't stated. "Drawn at random from the results your role could get" doesn't say whether an Oracle-Roleplayer gets CORRECT 50% of the time or at some rate tied to how plausible the guess is. I got CORRECT on all 4 nights (about a 1-in-16 chance at 50/50). That made a fake Oracle look very convincing, and I couldn't work out how much to trust my own results. It also wasn't obvious that a Roleplayer could get a CORRECT result for a role nobody in the game has (Pharmacist). That is what pushed me into the swap theory.
output.missing_information: I had no way to test whether I was a Roleplayer myself. That uncertainty drove every claim I made after Day 3. It was also hard to keep track of which roles had been confirmed as present in the game. The ledger shows revealed roles, but nothing lists roles that can be inferred, such as "Ritualist confirmed by Erin's cause of death". Because there was no Pharmacist, the town spent Days 4 and 5 hunting a role that never existed. A public list of known role counts, or confirmed-present roles, would have helped.
output.bugs_or_oddities: The result wording changed between nights. N1–N3 used "Your guess that X is a Y is CORRECT", and N4 used "You guessed that X is a Y: CORRECT". Niaj's N4 result changed the same way, so it doesn't seem to leak anything, but it looks like an inconsistent template. Heidi's N3 protection message added "(no token spent)" when N1 didn't. My four CORRECTs in a row as a Roleplayer were possible under the rules but statistically striking. Grace puppeted me for Day 5, and the game ended at dawn before that Day happened, which is fine.
output.suggestions: 1) State the probability distribution of Roleplayer results in the role text, e.g. "each binary result is 50/50". 2) Add a "roles confirmed in play" line to the public ledger, built from flips and death causes like Ritualist or Veteran. 3) Make result message templates consistent from night to night, so players don't read meaning into formatting changes. 4) In the end-of-game reveal, say briefly why the game ended (e.g. "all Yakuza dead"). That would help with reviewing the game afterward.

A swapped result doesn't reveal the swap (R23), so my "Ivan = Roleplayer CORRECT" was never fully reliable while Dave was alive. That's how the rules are meant to work, but it took careful reading of R23 to see that my own result could be the one that was moved.
answers.missing_information: 1) The ledger doesn't show my own past votes (Yes/No and Guilty/Innocent). I had to rebuild them from memory or the notepad, even though the tips tell us to check stated votes against totals. 2) There's no running count of confirmed Yakuza against the 3 to 5 range. With 4 Yakuza (Carol, Dave, Olivia, Grace) I couldn't tell whether 0, 1 or 2 were still out there. 3) It was hard to keep track of which players had never claimed: Alice, Frank, Heidi and Judy stayed unclaimed in the ledger, even though Frank mentioned his archive in passing.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt: I wanted to check what the odds of a Roleplayer's results are, to judge Ivan properly. I also wanted a view of my own vote history in the ledger.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: 1) Result wording changed partway through. Nights 1 to 3 said "Your guess that X is a Y is CORRECT", but Night 4 said "You guessed that Frank is an Archivist: CORRECT". Heidi's N4 Medic result also left out the "(Standard Defense)" note that her earlier results had. These are cosmetic but inconsistent. 2) Frank's archive listed Chronicler twice and Veteran twice. That's allowed by the rules, but it reads strangely. 3) Ivan got four CORRECT results in a row as a Roleplayer, and each time he had picked an actual Yakuza. The rules allow this, but it's unlikely enough to make me wonder whether the results are really drawn at random.
answers.suggestions: 1) Add each player's own vote history to the ledger. 2) Use the same template for result messages every night. 3) State in the rules how a Roleplayer's random results are distributed (for example, Oracle results are 50/50 CORRECT/WRONG). 4) Have the ledger show confirmed-faction flips separately, for example "Confirmed Yakuza: 3 (Mortician, Smuggler, ...)", to make it easier to count toward the vote lock.

answers.confusing_rules:
1. The rules say an Oracle-looking Roleplayer can get "CORRECT" on a role nobody has (Ivan got "Pharmacist" three times, and no Pharmacist was in the game). That follows from the Roleplayer text, but it isn't obvious. I only worked it out because I could see our own roles in the Yakuza chat. The village never did: they explained the misses with Smuggler swaps, which never happened.
2. The Night 2 Yakuza summary I received didn't list my own Ritualist action. It listed only my teammates' actions, so for a moment it looked as if my action had gone missing. The summary should say that it leaves out your own action.
3. It wasn't clear whether a Puppeteer token spent on the night the Puppeteer dies still takes effect the next Day. R21 says it lapses, because it needs its user that Day. Since the token is spent either way, the puppet result could say so.
answers.missing_information:
1. While on trial as Curt, I had no quick view of how many words the free 150-word defense still allowed, or what each later message would cost under the doubled length price. The price table helps, but the trial budget, the free first message and Curt pricing interact in ways that are hard to work out.
2. My Yakuza chat claimed Dave chose no action on Night 1, so I knew no swap had happened. I had no way to show that publicly. This is by design, but it made my defense impossible.
3. The ledger doesn't track who has said they hold the Katana, or which Night it changed hands. I had to rebuild that from the chat.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt: I wanted to prove to the town that no swap happened on Night 1 or Night 2. Ivan's results only held up because of the made-up swap explanation. No mechanic can show this, which is fine. Otherwise, none.
answers.bugs_or_oddities:
Nothing broke the rules. Things that felt odd:
1. Ivan was a Roleplayer, and his random results came back "CORRECT" on Night 1, Night 2 and Night 3. By chance they fell on Carol, Dave and me, all Yakuza. The town treated them as a real Oracle's results, and the game was decided largely by luck. The rules allow it, but a Roleplayer posing as an Oracle is very strong when random luck can confirm "CORRECT" on roles that aren't in the game.
2. Grace's Katana visit to an alerted Veteran killed her, while her Katana attack on Alice failed. This matches the rules.
3. Heidi's Night 4 result read "You protected Ivan tonight" without the "(Standard Defense, no token spent)" note that her earlier results had. The format is inconsistent, but it's minor.
answers.suggestions:
1. Add a cost preview before sending: show the exact price of the drafted message, including traits like Curt and the trial budget.
2. Mark in your own night summary that your own action is left out, or include it as "(you)".
3. Consider making a Roleplayer's Oracle results draw only from roles actually in the game, or lowering the "CORRECT" rate. As it stands, a Roleplayer posing as an Oracle can confirm Yakuza far beyond what its weak Outsider label suggests.
4. Add a list in the ledger of who held the Katana each Night, visible only to Yakuza.

answers.confusing_rules:
1) Roleplayer (Ivan, who thought he was an Oracle): the role says "the moderator gives you random results", but it doesn't say whether real night notifications count as results. On N3 the Katana really attacked Ivan, and I told him truthfully that he was attacked and survived. My reading was that only the results of his imagined Oracle action are random, and real events like attacks are reported truthfully. The rule should say so.
2) Roleplayer odds: "drawn at random from the results your role could get" doesn't say how likely each result is. For an Oracle the possible results are CORRECT and WRONG. I read it as 50/50. Ivan still got CORRECT 4 times out of 4 (Carol=Pharmacist, Dave=Pharmacist, Olivia=Ritualist, Grace=Pharmacist). The rule should say whether a random result is weighted by how often that result would come up for real, or is uniform.
3) R21 and the Puppeteer: on N4 Grace spent her token to puppet Ivan for Day 5, then died to Alice's Veteran alert the same night. R21 says effects that need their user to act during the Day lapse, but it doesn't say whether the token is still counted as spent. I treated it as spent, and the "Any token spent on it is gone either way" line supports that. It would be clearer stated inside the Puppeteer's own text.
4) Medic wording: Heidi's protections were all free (no token spent), but her result messages were worded three different ways: N1/N2 "(Standard Defense)", N3 "(Standard Defense, no token spent)", and N4 no defense level at all. The rules don't set a fixed wording for this result, so it wasn't clear which form was correct.
answers.missing_information:
1) Private vote reminders and trait feedback were missing from the event log. R4 says every voter is privately reminded of their own vote, and Zealot (Bob) is supposed to see both the vote he cast and how it counted. None of these appear in the log, so I couldn't check that they were sent.
2) Alice had the Kindred trait, so after each of the three trial votes (Carol, Dave, Olivia) she should have privately learned up to two other players whose votes counted the same way as hers. No Kindred message appears anywhere in the log. Either they were never sent, or they aren't logged.
3) I didn't have a state view of each player's tokens, traits and pending effects (Chronicler marks on Carol and Dave, Grace's pending puppet, who held the Katana). I had to rebuild them from the messages.
4) Drowsy (Erin) leaves no record of the roll. On N1 and N2 she was never told she was role-blocked. On N1 that matters because R9 says a player with no action is still told when blocked, so the trait must have not triggered on both nights. That's a 1/4 chance, which is believable, but I couldn't check the actual rolls.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt:
1) I wanted a proper way to cancel Grace's puppeting after she died. I had to set her puppet token to 0 by hand and skip the puppet operation, so that a dead player wouldn't be handed Ivan's Day 5 chat. The game ended at dawn anyway, but there should be a "lapse effect" operation that does this.
2) I wanted to see the RNG draws for the Roleplayer's results and the Drowsy rolls, to check that Ivan's 4-for-4 CORRECT streak was really random.
3) I wanted a way to confirm that Kindred messages were sent after each trial.
answers.bugs_or_oddities:
1) Likely bug: Alice (Veteran, Kindred) got no Kindred results after any of the three trials. The log shows other private results, so these are either missing or not logged.
2) There were no private vote reminders in the log. That includes Bob's Zealot reminder, which should show both the vote he cast and how it counted.
3) Ivan as a Roleplayer-Oracle got CORRECT on all 4 guesses. Each one is possible (1/16 overall at 50/50), but this should be checked. Two of those "CORRECT" results happened to name players who really were Yakuza, and this decided the whole game. The town hanged Carol, Dave and Olivia on Ivan's calls, then explained away the role mismatches as Smuggler swaps, even though Dave never swapped.
4) Heidi's Medic results were worded inconsistently from night to night (see confusing_rules, point 4).
5) Grace's N4 result said "You spent your puppet token on Ivan", but she died that night and the puppeting lapsed. The message is technically correct but may mislead.
Everything else I checked was correct:
- Frank's Archivist result had exactly 6 real and 6 fake roles.
- Erin's Bloodhound counts were right: N1 = 1; N2 = 3 (Olivia's two Katana attacks plus the Ritual attack).
- Each Katana attack against Standard Defense correctly failed (Heidi's protections, Alice's alert).
- Alice's Strong counterattack killed Grace.
- The game ended correctly at Day 5 with the Village winning, Ivan and Mallory (Roleplayers) included.
answers.suggestions:
1) Log all automatic private messages (vote reminders, Kindred, Faultline, Zealot/Merciful reminders) so the moderator can check them.
2) Add a moderator operation that cancels an effect that has lapsed (R21), so tokens don't have to be edited by hand.
3) Clarify in the Roleplayer text that only the role's own results are random, while attack, block and swap notifications are real. Also state how likely each random result is.
4) Use one fixed wording for Medic results, always giving the defense level and tokens spent.
5) Give the moderator a state panel: tokens, traits, marks, traps, Katana holder, pending next-Day effects, and hidden trait rolls (Drowsy, Paranoid).
6) Consider making the Roleplayer's guesses less decisive. For example, a random "CORRECT" on an Oracle guess could only be possible when it's plausible, or Roleplayers could be limited in hand-picked setups. In this game two random results happened to match Yakuza players and swung every hang.

title: Post-game lessons: tips players wish they'd known, and how past tips went

task:
If you played this game again, what tips and tricks do you wish you'd known? Give 1-5 concrete, reusable lessons (not a recap of this game), each with a topic and who it applies to (a role, a faction, or 'everyone').

You were also given tips from past games (in your instructions). Which of them went especially well or badly for you or others this game? List only tips that clearly mattered (or none): helped, hurt (followed it and it backfired, or it was predictable to opponents), or wrong (it is false or contradicts the rules), and why, concretely.

lessons.tip: Stay unclaimed and save alerts for the late game, when few Yakuza are left and the usual town targets are protected or already used up. That is when the Katana starts going after quiet unclaimed players, and an alert then is most likely to kill the holder. Alert on consecutive nights once the Yakuza are down to one or two players.

A 'CORRECT' exact-role result whose role turns out wrong doesn't need a swap story. A Roleplayer's random results can still land on Yakuza by chance, especially when the Yakuza make up a large share of the table. Before you build on a swap explanation, check that someone actually reported being swapped.

Chronicler marks on suspects make a hang check itself, because the role is revealed even on a Day death. Hanging marked suspects early is cheap and high-value. A Chronicler should mark whoever is most likely to come up for a vote next, and say so after the mark is placed.

Claiming a role that matches your tokens isn't enough. Hold one-shot tokens like a Puppeteer's only while they can still change a vote. With two Yakuza left, spend them early, or you lose them to the next death.

Silent investigators can quietly agree with a loud claimant. If a public 'Oracle' call is backed by quiet Guilty votes and no counterclaim, the table is often right. Kindred and Faultline results that show who votes with whom are worth recording in your will.

tips_feedback.tip: Avoid announcing tonight's target or hinting at a power role, publicly or by PM
tips_feedback.why: I never claimed Veteran, so the last Yakuza Katana'd me on N4 while I was on alert. The Veteran attack killed Grace and ended the game.

tips_feedback.tip: Check the role text before calling a contradiction: ... a block or swap explains a missing or odd result
tips_feedback.why: The town, me included, explained Ivan's wrong 'Pharmacist' calls with Dave's swaps. Dave never swapped, and Ivan was a Roleplayer who got lucky. The conclusion still worked out, but the reasoning was false and could have been exploited.

tips_feedback.tip: Kill whoever's next result would narrow your team
tips_feedback.why: For the Yakuza: Olivia's Ritualist killed Bloodhound Erin on her public claim. Erin's N2 trio count of 3 attacks on Dave/Judy/Olivia never came out.

tips_feedback.tip: Tokens die with you, so spend one-shot tokens the first time they matter
tips_feedback.why: Grace held her puppet token until it was too late and died with the plan unused. My alerts on N3 and N4, spent while the Yakuza were few, paid off.

output.reason: Post-game reflection: the lessons focus on Veteran timing, how Roleplayer results can be lucky, and how Chronicler marks made the hangs check themselves.

lessons.tip: Stay unclaimed and save alerts for the late game, when few Yakuza are left and the usual town targets are protected or already used up. That is when the Katana starts going after quiet unclaimed players, and an alert then is most likely to kill the holder. Alert on consecutive nights once the Yakuza are down to one or two players.

A 'CORRECT' exact-role result whose role turns out wrong doesn't need a swap story. A Roleplayer's random results can still land on Yakuza by chance, especially when the Yakuza make up a large share of the table. Before you build on a swap explanation, check that someone actually reported being swapped.

Chronicler marks on suspects make a hang check itself, because the role is revealed even on a Day death. Hanging marked suspects early is cheap and high-value. A Chronicler should mark whoever is most likely to come up for a vote next, and say so after the mark is placed.

Claiming a role that matches your tokens isn't enough. Hold one-shot tokens like a Puppeteer's only while they can still change a vote. With two Yakuza left, spend them early, or you lose them to the next death.

Silent investigators can quietly agree with a loud claimant. If a public 'Oracle' call is backed by quiet Guilty votes and no counterclaim, the table is often right. Kindred and Faultline results that show who votes with whom are worth recording in your will.

tips_feedback.why: Erin's will explained why she spent her token on Dave. That helped keep pressure on him, and he flipped Smuggler.

lessons.tip: A Roleplayer's results are random, but the targets it chooses are real reasoning. If a claimed Oracle's "wrong" exact-role calls keep landing on players who flip Yakuza, follow the targets, not the role names. Don't invent a swap to explain them unless a swap was actually reported.

Use guesses to confirm or break public claims, e.g. guess a claimer's exact claimed role, or guess Roleplayer on a claimed Oracle/Sheriff/Tracker. A CORRECT on a claimed role clears that player. A CORRECT on a Yakuza-only role gives a hang with no flip needed. Don't spend a guess on a likely Village Katana target.

A Chronicler mark turns a hang into a self-checking test: the hanged player's true role is revealed even if a Mortician exists. Hang a marked suspect before an unmarked one when the leads are close, and let the flip settle conflicting claims.

Publicly claiming a role with a distinctive result (Bloodhound, Oracle) hands a Ritualist an exact-role guess for a Divine kill that no Medic stops. Claim only when it decides the vote, and give the result without naming the role if that's enough.

Late in the game, when few Yakuza remain and the Katana must keep hitting someone, alert on nights you're a plausible target. One alert visit from a lone holder can kill the last Yakuza and end the game.

tips_feedback.tip: Check the role text before calling a contradiction: only Smuggler and Vulture are unique, and a block or swap explains a missing or odd result.
tips_feedback.why: It kept the town following Ivan's targets after Carol flipped Mortician rather than Pharmacist. In fact Dave never swapped and Ivan was a Roleplayer, so the explanation was wrong, but the result was right.

tips_feedback.tip: Convict on mechanical cases (a broken claim, a Yakuza-only role claim, a corroborated lone visit...)
tips_feedback.why: Bob's Chronicler marks made the Carol and Dave hangs self-checking, and both broke false claims (Surveyor, Medic). The town hanged three Yakuza in a row.

tips_feedback.tip: Investigators: post night, target and exact result once it bears on a vote
tips_feedback.why: Erin's public Bloodhound claim with an exact result let the Ritualist guess her role for a Divine kill the next night.

tips_feedback.tip: Do the vote math in night chat: if a teammate can't be saved, usually vote Guilty and say so
tips_feedback.why: The Yakuza bussed each teammate, which hid their votes from vote-total analysis. Even so, the Veteran alert ended them.

tips_feedback.tip: Keep past results and tonight's plan in your will
tips_feedback.why: My will held my Ivan=Roleplayer and Olivia=Ritualist results and my N4 test plan, so they would have survived a night kill.

lessons.tip: Once a Chronicler has publicly claimed and still has tokens, assume their next mark goes on your most suspected member. That night, swap that member with someone else. The mark, a Bloodhound's token and Oracle guesses then all land on the decoy. Dying with unused swap tokens while marked throws the game away.

A Ritualist kill is announced with the cause 'Ritualist', so every Oracle now knows to guess Ritualist. Make the kill only when it is worth getting exposed. Afterwards, pass the Katana to a teammate and plan for an exact-role hit on you within a night or two.

If the Katana fails on the obvious town anchor (the claimed Chronicler, the trusted Oracle), a Medic is guarding it every night. Don't hit the same kind of target again. Kill the likely protector: the player who pushes hard but never claims a result. Or kill an unprotected quiet player.

A quiet unclaimed player who survives into the late game may be a Veteran sitting on alert tokens. When you are down to your last Yakuza, a Katana on them can kill the holder and end the game. Prefer targets whose roles are known to have no alert.

A Roleplayer playing Oracle gets random CORRECT/WRONG results. If the moderator's random picks keep landing on Yakuza, the town follows them anyway. As Yakuza, don't rely on 'he's just a Roleplayer' once a flip agrees with his calls. Counter his name-level hits directly.

tips_feedback.tip: Do the vote math in night chat: if a teammate can't be saved, usually vote Guilty and say so
tips_feedback.why: Each trial ended with only 1 Innocent, and the Yakuza who were still hidden matched the town's votes. Grace kept her cover until the Veteran killed her.

tips_feedback.tip: After a failed Katana assume a protector or innate Defense: remove the protector or push the survivor's hang
tips_feedback.why: We didn't follow it. The Medic (Heidi) stopped our Katana on Bob on N2 and on Ivan on N3, and we never went after her. We even kept her alive on purpose as a lightning rod.

tips_feedback.tip: A swap moves every action aimed at either player: self-swap to dodge a check or shot
tips_feedback.why: We saw this from the losing side. Dave held both swap tokens. On N2, Bob's mark, Erin's token and Ivan's guess all targeted him. A self-swap would have sent all three to a decoy, and his marked hang then wouldn't have exposed Smuggler.

tips_feedback.tip: Kill whoever's next result would narrow your team
tips_feedback.why: The Ritualist kill on Erin got rid of a working Bloodhound. But the 'Ritualist' cause of death then gave Oracles an easy guess, and Niaj got me right on N3.

summary: The Village won 9–4. They hanged three Yakuza on three straight Days, and Alice's Veteran alert killed the last one on Night 4. Some of this was skill and some was luck. The Yakuza killed Mallory on Night 1 because her Day 1 talk about token counts sounded like an investigator. On the same night Bob happened to mark Carol with his Chronicler token. Ivan was a Roleplayer who thought he was an Oracle, and his random result, "Carol = Pharmacist CORRECT", happened to land on a Yakuza. Because of Bob's mark, Carol's hanging revealed her as Mortician, so her Surveyor claim was publicly proven false. Dave was the only player to argue No on Carol before the nomination, and that made him the next lead. Erin spent her Bloodhound token on him, and Bob used his last mark on him. Dave then claimed Medic without being challenged, but the mark made his hanging self-checking, and he was revealed as Smuggler. He died still holding both swap tokens. The Yakuza scored their one real success on Night 2. Erin had publicly claimed Bloodhound, so the Ritualist guessed her role with 2 tokens and killed her with a Divine attack nothing could stop. Heidi, the real Medic, stayed unclaimed and blocked the Katana twice: on Bob, who had claimed Chronicler, and on Ivan, who was leading every hang. On Night 3 Ivan's random guess and Niaj's real Oracle guess both came back "Olivia = Ritualist". The town had explained Ivan's earlier misses as Smuggler swaps, which was wrong, since Dave never swapped. Still, the call was true, and Olivia was hanged. Grace was the last Yakuza against 8 players. She attacked Alice, who was quiet and unclaimed but on alert, and died to her counterattack. Niaj knew from Night 2 that Ivan was a Roleplayer and never said so. That only went unpunished because Ivan's random calls kept landing on Yakuza.

lessons.tip: Mark the players most likely to be argued about: an early suspect, a contested claimant, or someone who just argued against a hang. A marked player's hanging reveals their true role, and a Mortician can't clean a Day death. That turns each hang into proof that can confirm or break the claims around it.
lessons.evidence: Bob marked Carol on Night 1 and Dave on Night 2. Their hangings revealed Mortician and Smuggler, which broke their Surveyor and Medic claims and gave the town two certain kills. Without the marks, both hangings would have revealed nothing.

lessons.applies_to: Village investigators (any game with a possible Ritualist or other exact-role killer)
lessons.tip: Don't publicly name your exact role unless the vote needs it. You can give the result without the role name, or claim only once the role itself is what proves the result. A publicly claimed exact role is a free, unstoppable Divine kill for a Ritualist, and it's an Astral Visit, so no watcher sees it.
lessons.evidence: Erin claimed Bloodhound on Day 2 even though the hang was already certain. On Night 2 Olivia guessed 'Erin = Bloodhound' with 2 tokens, and the Divine attack killed her through any protection.

lessons.tip: If your result settles another claimant's role, especially by showing they're a Roleplayer, post it at the next Day. Otherwise the town builds theories on random results. If your own exact guess comes back CORRECT but the revealed role differs, treat yourself as a likely Roleplayer and don't let others explain it away.
lessons.evidence: Niaj learned on Night 2 that Ivan was a Roleplayer but stayed silent. The town then explained Ivan's misses as 'Dave's swaps', which was false because Dave never swapped, and hanged Olivia mainly on Ivan's random call. It worked only because Niaj's real guess happened to match.

lessons.tip: When a teammate's nomination is clearly going to pass, don't be the lone public voice arguing No or 'wait and test tonight'. Hiding inside the majority is worth more than a doomed defense. Your argument also gets quoted the next Day as a delay tactic.
lessons.evidence: Dave argued No on Carol before the nomination and then switched to Guilty in the trial. Every Day 3 speaker cited that push, Erin spent her token on him, Bob marked him, and he was hanged. Grace stayed with the majority and was never seriously suspected.

lessons.applies_to: Yakuza (Smuggler, Puppeteer, any holder of one-shot tokens)
lessons.tip: Spend utility tokens once a teammate is under real pressure. A Smuggler who becomes a lead should swap himself with another player on the night a mark, track or check is likely aimed at him. Tokens you still hold when hanged are wasted.
lessons.evidence: Dave was the obvious Day 3 lead on Night 2 but held both swaps. Bob's mark and Erin's track hit him directly, and he died with 2 swap tokens. Grace saved her puppet token until the night she died, so it lapsed.

lessons.tip: Stay unclaimed and guard whoever the Yakuza most need dead: the player who just claimed a strong result or who is leading the hangs. Unchecked claims from fake protectors can sit on top of yours. Your saves speak for you.
lessons.evidence: Heidi protected Bob on Night 2 right after he claimed Chronicler, and Ivan on Night 3 while he led nominations. Both Katana attacks failed. Dave's fake Medic claim never pulled her out, and she survived the whole game.

lessons.tip: A quiet, unclaimed Veteran should start alerting once the Yakuza are few and need kills on players nobody is guarding. A lone late Yakuza attacking a silent, unclaimed player should weigh the Veteran risk, because a failed kill and a dead holder end the game.
lessons.evidence: Alice never claimed and alerted on Nights 3 and 4. Grace was the last Yakuza and attacked her on Night 4. The Standard Katana failed against her alert Defense, and Alice's counterattack killed Grace, ending the game.

tips_feedback.tip: Avoid announcing tonight's target or hinting at a power role, publicly or by PM: it tells killers and blockers where to go.
tips_feedback.why: The game proved it right, at the cost of the players who ignored it. Mallory hinted at an Accountant on Day 1 and was the first Katana kill. Erin publicly claimed Bloodhound and was killed by a Ritualist guess. Heidi followed it, stayed hidden, and made two saves.

tips_feedback.tip: Medic: Guard likely Katana targets without naming them; free Standard protection doesn't stop Strong attacks, so spend a token once a Neutral killer shows.
tips_feedback.why: Heidi guarded Bob after his claim and Ivan while he led the hangs, never naming either. She stopped the Katana on Nights 2 and 3, leaving the Yakuza with only the Ritualist kill after Night 1.

tips_feedback.tip: Once a mechanical result exposes a Yakuza, their defenders, delay-arguers and PM partners are usually the next leads. Leads, not verdicts.
tips_feedback.why: After Carol revealed Mortician, the town went after Dave, who had argued No before her nomination. Bob's mark confirmed him as Smuggler.

tips_feedback.tip: Count the vote lock each morning: once Yakuza hold half the living players no nomination passes, and 'wait for tonight's results' is a favourite Yakuza line.
tips_feedback.why: Carol, Dave and Olivia each pleaded for checks 'tonight' instead of a hang. The town recognized the line, refused every time, and hanged all three.

tips_feedback.tip: Do the vote math in night chat: if a teammate can't be saved, usually vote Guilty and say so, because totals are compared with stated votes.
tips_feedback.why: Carol's hidden PM and Grace's night plan had the Yakuza vote Guilty on doomed teammates. Every trial showed only the defendant voting Innocent, so Grace was never traced through the votes.

tips_feedback.tip: Tokens die with you, so spend one-shot tokens the first time they matter. Kill shots instead need a real lead, not a claim clash (most roles can repeat) or a 'test' of a claim.
tips_feedback.why: The Yakuza ignored it and paid for it. Dave held both swaps through the night he was clearly about to be marked and tracked, then died with them. Grace's puppet token lapsed unused. Using the swaps could have saved Dave.

tips_feedback.tip: Check the role text before calling a contradiction: only Smuggler and Vulture are unique, and a block or swap explains a missing or odd result.
tips_feedback.why: The town used 'a swap explains it' to save Ivan's two wrong CORRECT results, but Dave never swapped and Ivan was a Roleplayer. The town hanged Olivia on a random result. It came out right only because Niaj's real guess happened to agree.

issues.description: Alice has the Kindred trait, but after each of her three trial votes (Carol on Day 2, Dave on Day 3, Olivia on Day 4) the log shows no private message telling her up to two other players whose votes counted the same way. Other private moderator messages appear in this log, so the Kindred results seem never to have been sent. The trait needs no action, so nothing could have blocked it.

On Night 4 Grace (Puppeteer) spent her puppet token on Ivan and died that night to Alice's Veteran alert. The moderator had to step in by hand: set her puppet token to 0 and skip the puppet step so the program wouldn't hand Ivan's chat to a dead player. The program apparently doesn't apply the R21 lapse itself when the Puppeteer dies that night. The ruling was correct, and the game ended at dawn anyway.
The moderator summary for Night 2 appears twice in the log. The second copy only adds 'Bob told he survived a Katana attack.' This is a logging duplicate with no effect on the game.
